description: Helps you decide how to win against each competitor: it takes your product and the competitors you name, and returns one battle card per competitor built from your strengths, weaknesses, competitor details, objections, wins and losses. Each competitor detail goes to the competitor it names, each objection gets its own answer, and strengths and gaps taken from wins and losses stay in your own words. Read-only for business data. It needs no sign-in and stores no inputs or outputs. Hosted usage metadata is recorded. Missing required fields or invalid values return an error naming what to supply or correct. Use this instead of competitive_trap_setter when you need complete battle cards across the competitors you supply.

business_model.description: Optional: how you earn revenue, so the advice fits it (saas, services, connectivity, transactions, marketplace, hardware_software or investment). Leave it out and the tool reads it from your other inputs and says how it read it. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "saas".

common_objections.description: Sales objections you hear (comma-separated). E.g., 'too expensive, missing X feature, competitor has better Y'. Format is text.

competitor_details.description: Optional: Any known details about competitors, one per line or separated by semicolons. E.g., 'Competitor A is cheaper; Competitor B targets enterprise'. Each detail goes to the competitor it names. Format is text.

competitors.description: Competitor names, comma-separated. You get one battle card for each competitor named. Format is text. For example, "the current manual review process".

industry.description: Optional: your own company's sector, so the answer uses the usual buyers, measures and objections for what you sell. Leave it out and the tool reads the sector from your other inputs and names what it read. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

recent_losses.description: Why you lost deals to competitors: used as your gaps when none are given. Format is text. For example, "two deals paused after budget review".

recent_wins.description: Why customers chose you over competitors: used as your strengths when none are given. Format is text. For example, "finance teams chose the documented exception process".

your_product.description: Your product name and brief description. Format is text. For example, "invoice review service".

your_sector.description: Optional: your company's own industry (not your customers'). When given, it decides the sector notes; when left out, the tool reads it from your words and stays neutral if they are unclear. Format is text using one of the listed labels. For example, "logistics_tech".

your_strengths.description: Optional: what you do better, comma-separated. Taken from your wins, in your own words, if not provided. Format is text. For example, "checks invoice exceptions before approval".

your_weaknesses.description: Optional: where competitors beat you, comma-separated. Taken from your losses, in your own words, if not provided. Format is text. For example, "handoffs require manual reconciliation".
